title: CAAD: Causality-Aware Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection via Multi-Scale Alignment and Structural Causal Consistency

problem.claim: Complex industrial systems require precise anomaly detection and diagnosis to maintain operational integrity.

gap.claim: Many existing methods focus on temporal representation similarity while overlooking disruptions in internal causal relationships associated with failures and latent anomalies.

contributions.claim: CAAD reframes anomaly detection as continuous verification of Granger-causality consistency through exogenous variables.
CAAD models exogenous time-series variables as residuals and identifies anomalies through significant deviations attributed to external interventions.
CAAD combines multi-scale alignment with a gradient-based matrix to model system dynamics and monitor internal causal relationship breakdowns.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present CAAD as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world industrial datasets reportedly show high-precision anomaly detection.
The authors report that CAAD outperforms most state-of-the-art baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Industrial-system operational integrity depends on precise anomaly detection and diagnosis.
Existing approaches often overlook causal-relationship disruptions by emphasizing temporal representation similarity.
CAAD formulates anomaly detection as continuous checking of Granger-causality consistency using exogenous variables.
The framework represents exogenous variables as residuals and uses multi-scale alignment plus gradient-based causal monitoring.
The authors report that causal-deviation measurements capture subtle shifts and that CAAD performs strongly against state-of-the-art baselines on real-world industrial datasets.
